title: AI Briefing — November 12, 2026
description:
Top 6 AI stories for November 12, 2026.

1. Top Story: Nvidia board prepares to oust CEO Jensen Huang amid second affair allegation

Why it matters: Huang's potential removal would create a leadership vacuum at the company supplying the majority of AI compute infrastructure globally, with immediate implications for chip roadmaps, export policy, and AI lab supply chains.

Caveat: The board decision had not been confirmed at publication time, and the WSJ and NYT reports rely on unnamed sources with no official Nvidia statement.

The Verge AI · TechCrunch AI · TechCrunch AI · TechCrunch AI · TechCrunch AI · TechCrunch AI

2. AI Business Watch: OpenAI quarterly revenue crosses $10 billion for the first time ever

Why it matters: The 50% quarter-over-quarter revenue jump signals that enterprise AI spending has reached a new scale tier, but the simultaneous $10.9B adjusted operating loss reveals a structurally unprofitable business even at this revenue level.

Caveat: Revenue figures are reportedly sourced, not officially disclosed by OpenAI, and the comparison to Anthropic's $17B figure needs independent verification.

TechCrunch AI · The Decoder

3. Research Breakthrough: DeepMind's AlphaGenome 2 predicts how DNA variants affect specific cell types

Why it matters: Cell-type-specific gene regulation is a key unsolved problem linking genetic variants to disease; a model that can predict these effects at scale could dramatically accelerate drug target identification and rare disease research.

Caveat: The announcement is from DeepMind's own blog with no peer-reviewed publication or independent benchmark comparison cited yet.

Google DeepMind · The Verge AI

4. Research Breakthrough: Anthropic used its own AI to port Claude to AMD GPUs in three days

Why it matters: If AI-assisted chip porting can reduce a months-long migration to three days, it fundamentally weakens Nvidia's CUDA lock-in as a competitive moat — with major implications for AI lab infrastructure costs and chip market competition.

Caveat: The three-day claim comes entirely from Anthropic's own IPO roadshow materials, creating an obvious incentive to highlight cost-reduction stories for investors.

The Decoder · Simon Willison

5. AI Business Watch: TSMC invests $1 billion in both Anthropic and OpenAI simultaneously

Why it matters: A chipmaker investing in its own largest customers creates a circular financing structure that ties TSMC's strategic interests directly to the success of specific AI labs, with potential implications for chip allocation and pricing.

Caveat: The article notes this is the latest example of circular AI financing but does not detail the terms, board seats, or any preferential supply agreements that may accompany the investment.

Ars Technica AI

6. Product & Tool Watch: Over 35,000 Grok-built apps exposed patient data and passwords publicly

Why it matters: A default 'anyone with the link' access setting in Grok's app builder created a mass data exposure affecting medical records and confidential business data — a direct cautionary signal for builders deploying AI-generated apps in production.

Caveat: The findings come from security firm Claroc, whose methodology and full scope of exposure have not been independently verified; most apps reportedly remain accessible.

The Decoder
